questions.q: A live batch shows the same customer features as training, but customers now cancel for different reasons and the model's AUC collapses. What is this?
options: Concept drift: the relationship between inputs and outcome changed
Data drift: the input distributions changed
A high PSI on every feature
Overfitting to the test set
questions.explain: The inputs look unchanged but their meaning changed, which is concept drift. It is invisible to input-only checks.

questions.q: Which kind of drift can be detected without waiting for ground-truth labels?
options: Concept drift only
Data drift, by comparing feature distributions
Neither, both need labels
Both, using accuracy
questions.explain: Comparing live feature distributions to training (PSI, KS) needs no labels. Measuring accuracy and spotting concept drift does.

questions.q: In the lesson's PSI function, why are the bin edges computed from the training (reference) data?
options: So the live data can never contain missing values
Because scipy requires it
So every batch is compared against the same fixed yardstick
To make the score always fall between 0 and 1
questions.explain: Using training quantiles as fixed bins means each new batch is compared against the same reference, so scores are comparable over time. PSI is not bounded by 1.

questions.q: With thousands of rows, a KS test returns p < 0.001 for a tiny, harmless shift. What is the sensible response?
options: Retrain immediately
Ignore KS completely and never monitor that feature
Assume the labels are wrong
Also look at the effect size (PSI or the KS statistic) before alerting
questions.explain: Large samples make p-values overreact. Alerting on effect size, such as PSI or the KS statistic, is more robust.

questions.q: In the lesson, the data-drift batch (days_idle PSI 0.889) scored AUC 0.728 against 0.754 on normal data. What does that show?
options: Input drift is always harmless
Large input drift does not necessarily mean a large accuracy loss
AUC cannot be computed on drifted data
PSI values below 0.25 are impossible
questions.explain: The inputs moved a lot but the model's ranking largely survived. Input drift is a warning to investigate, not proof of harm, so you also monitor outcomes.
